gloss: to drag out; to haul out

definitions.gloss: to drag out; to haul out
definitions.explanation: to forcibly pull something or someone out of a place by dragging

definitions.gloss: to force out; to bring to light
definitions.explanation: to compel someone to come out or to expose something hidden

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}をソファの{下|した}から{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I dragged the dog out from under the sofa.

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{荷物|にもつ}を{車|くるま}から{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To haul heavy luggage out of the car.

examples.japanese: {倒|たお}れた{人|ひと}を{燃|も}えている{建物|たてもの}から{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}して{助|たす}けた。
examples.english: They dragged the collapsed person out of the burning building and saved them.

examples.japanese: {隠|かく}れていた{犯人|はんにん}を{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}した。
examples.english: They dragged out the hiding criminal.

examples.japanese: {真実|しんじつ}を{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}さなければならない。
examples.english: We must bring the truth to light.

examples.japanese: マスコミは{政治家|せいじか}の{過去|かこ}のスキャンダルを{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}して{報道|ほうどう}した。
examples.english: The media dug up and reported on the politician's past scandal.

notes:
A compound verb combining {引|ひ}きずる (to drag) and {出|だ}す (to take out). The physical sense implies forceful, rough pulling. The figurative sense conveys forcibly exposing something hidden or compelling someone reluctant to appear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犯人|はんにん}を{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}す — to drag out a criminal
- {真実|しんじつ}を{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}す — to drag out the truth
- {布団|ふとん}から{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}す — to drag someone out of bed
- スキャンダルを{引|ひ}きずり{出|だ}す — to unearth a scandal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引|ひ}っ{張|ぱ}り{出|だ}す — to pull out (less forceful, can be positive: "to recruit")
- {引|ひ}きずる — to drag (no directional element)
- {暴|あば}く — to expose, to reveal (secrets or wrongdoing)
